perspective:
From Maria Ortega’s available perspective:

- I know I am Maria Ortega, a Hispanic woman, a teacher with a master’s degree; I know my own thoughts, feelings, intentions, and actions.
- I know Cheryl Benallie as my colleague at the community center. We occasionally collaborate, are developing a friendship, and have discussed our different cultural backgrounds and personal experiences.
- I saw Cheryl stressed and overwhelmed by stacks of paperwork and planning for a new community outreach project. I offered to help because I had time. Cheryl accepted, saying it would be amazing and she could use the help.
- After helping Cheryl, I observed her handling responsibilities better and gaining confidence. In a staff meeting, I suggested Cheryl lead the next phase, citing her aptitude and commitment. I heard the Team Leader ask Cheryl about it. Cheryl thanked me for my confidence and said she was ready.
- I worried my suggestion might have overstepped. I approached Cheryl privately and told her I wanted to make sure she felt supported, not pressured. Cheryl told me she had been a bit surprised but appreciated my support and that my belief in her meant a lot.
- I felt relieved that Cheryl valued my honesty and support. I proposed that we co-lead the project. Cheryl agreed, saying it sounded fantastic, that my guidance had been invaluable, and that we make a great team.
- We successfully collaborated on several projects, strengthening our partnership. I felt joyful about our synergy. I asked Cheryl about teaming up for more future projects. Cheryl said she would love that, that working with me had been wonderful, and that she was excited about what we could achieve together.

I do not have access to Cheryl’s private thoughts, education, personality type, or other hidden details except what she directly told me or I observed.
